Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: No digital authentication function. The national ID card has a 2D barcode and MRZ field but no online/digital authentication capability. Analysts note the country 'lacks a national digital identity system' and no eKYC or online verification infrastructure is described in any source. Authentication remains physical/in-person only.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: No government portal authentication via national ID. While South Sudan launched an e-government system in 2019 and ordered digital transformation by 2026, no functional government portal using national ID for authentication has been documented. The World Bank (2023) described South Sudan's digital economy as 'very early stage' with absence of a clear ICT regulatory framework.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: No mechanism for individuals to access their own data. South Sudan has no data protection law, no data subject rights, and no portal or process for citizens to view, correct, or request deletion of ID data. Data Protection Africa confirms: 'Right of data subject to access a copy of their personal data: No law.'

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: No formal digital KYC enablement. While the national ID is cited as a document for banking and services, there is no eKYC infrastructure or API. The Jan 2026 DCRNPI directive mandates ID for banking but relies on physical document checks. No online KYC verification system linked to the national ID database is documented.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: General judicial oversight exists in South Sudan's legal system. The Transitional Constitution (2011) Article 22 protects privacy rights enforceable through courts. The Refugee Act 2012 provides for judicial appeals board for refugee status decisions. However, no ID-specific judicial oversight mechanism exists. Courts can hear general grievances but there is no specialized tribunal or mechanism for ID-related disputes.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Partial CRVS integration. The Civil Registry Act 2018 and Civil Registry Regulations (December 2024) establish a framework for linking civil registration to national ID. The UNECA presentation notes 'Strengthen the Interoperability with Health Sector' as a way forward, indicating current integration is incomplete. Birth registration coverage is ~35% (UNICEF). Integration between DCRNPI and birth/vital registration is planned but not fully operational.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: No formal data sharing rules exist. South Sudan has no data protection law, so there are no codified rules governing data sharing from the ID system. The Data Protection Africa fact sheet confirms no law governs cross-border data transfers or data processing. Inter-agency biometric data sharing has occurred informally (e.g., IOM-WFP in 2019) without a regulatory framework.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: No specific digital ID regulation exists. The Civil Registry Act 2018 covers civil registration broadly. The Cybercrimes and Computer Misuse Provisional Order 2021 addresses cybercrime but not digital identity specifically. A Data Protection Bill was announced for 2026 but has not been passed. No dedicated digital ID law found.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: South Sudan has no Data Protection Act. As of December 2025, the Minister of ICT announced a Data Protection Bill would be introduced in 2026 to complement the Cybercrime and Abuse of Computer Bill 2025. The Data Protection Africa fact sheet confirms: 'South Sudan currently has no data protection legislation.'

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: No Data Protection Authority exists. Data Protection Africa confirms there is 'no data protection authority yet appointed.' The National Communication Authority (NCA) handles cybersecurity but has no data protection mandate. No DPA is established or empowered to investigate, with no law providing for one.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The national ID card (Butaka Shakhsia) has legal proof status. In January 2026, DCRNPI Director General stated that the personal ID card 'will now be required for services including banking, land transactions and court processes.' The Nationality Act 2011 and Civil Registry Act 2018 provide legal recognition. The national ID card is described as evidence of citizenship for employment and formal transactions.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: South Sudan has a legal framework for civil registration and identity: the Nationality Act 2011, the Civil Registry Act 2018 (launched by President Kiir in 2019), and the Civil Registry Regulations adopted in December 2024. These provide the statutory basis for the national ID system under DCRNPI.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: A German company (MUHLBAUER) is the primary supplier/vendor for the national ID system. UNHCR and EU provide most operational support for ID card issuance. The January 2026 passport digital payment reform was 'supported by European Union services.' South Sudan government lacks domestic capacity to maintain the system independently, as confirmed by UNECA presentation citing 'lack of capacity (Institutional and personnel).'

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: Partial Ministry of Finance oversight. The January 2026 passport/ID payment digitization reform was implemented by the National Revenue Authority (NRA) to channel fees to suppliers and reduce leakage, indicating some financial oversight. However, the system has been plagued by mismanagement, with cash collected 'used elsewhere.' The World Bank PFM project (2022, $34M) is supporting financial oversight improvements. Full integration of ID revenues into transparent budget systems is not yet achieved.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: ID system is primarily externally funded. The EU/UNHCR partnership funded 17,400+ ID cards in 2024. Hold the Child project (UNHCR/EU-funded) supports civil registration pilots. World Bank IDA grants fund institutional capacity. The UNECA presentation lists 'Budgetary constraints' as a key challenge. Government called for a 'donor conference on civil registration financing.' Domestic revenue from ID fees has been mismanaged and is insufficient.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: Biometric data collection includes both fingerprints and iris scans. UNHCR mobile registration teams use biometric iris and fingerprint scanners. The World Bank EAC study notes the card includes a thumbprint image and biographic data. German vendor (MUHLBAUER) supplied the system.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: An electronic database exists for the national ID (DCRNPI issues cards linked to a database with photo and biographic data). However, the system is fragmented: the Jan 2026 passport digital payment announcement noted 'the lack of a real-time, integrated digital system' and papers/manual records remain prevalent. Multiple siloed databases exist (DCRNPI, UNHCR, WFP, IOM).

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: South Sudan launched a biometric national ID system in January 2012 under the Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passports and Immigration (DCRNPI). As of 2024, UNHCR/EU partnerships continue issuing ID cards (17,400+ issued in 2024). System is operational but only partially deployed nationwide due to infrastructure gaps, low coverage (~20% of population), and reliance on external support.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: No system interoperability. Analysts explicitly note that South Sudan 'still lacks a national digital identity system, forcing the government to rely on fragmented biometric databases rather than interoperable digital public goods.' The UNECA CRVS presentation lists 'Limited Coordination Mechanism among agencies' and 'Lack of harmonization of procedures' as key challenges.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: National ID is now required for banking as per the January 2026 DCRNPI directive stating the personal ID 'will now be required for services including banking.' However, practical enforcement is limited given only ~20% of the population holds an ID, and the banking sector remains small. The directive marks an intent to make it mandatory but full enforcement is not yet nationwide.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: There is a cost to obtain ID credentials. Applicants must pay approximately $20 in fees plus the cost of a blood test and two passport photographs. UNHCR reports this is a barrier for returnees and displaced persons. Revenue collection was previously in cash (now digital via bank in Jan 2026 reform), but costs remain. Birth certificate and witness requirements add further indirect costs.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: The personal ID card (Butaka Shakhsia) is issued only to adults aged 18 and above, as confirmed by the January 2026 DCRNPI statement. The World Bank EAC study noted 'age threshold 16 or 18 pending Parliament.' The nationality certificate is available to all ages. For the primary national ID card, eligibility threshold is 18+.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Enrollment is mandatory for some purposes. The national ID is required for formal employment, banking (as of Jan 2026 DCRNPI directive), land transactions and court processes. Wikipedia notes the ID is 'issued to every South Sudanese of at least eighteen years of age for purposes of employment or as required by a competent authority.' Not universally enforced but required for specific services.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: No evidence found that national ID is used for healthcare access in South Sudan. DCRNPI January 2026 directive references banking, land and court processes but not healthcare specifically. UNHCR and NGO health service delivery in South Sudan does not require national IDs. No source found documenting ID as required or accepted for healthcare access.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Some non-nationals are eligible for identity documents. Refugees receive refugee identity cards issued by the Commission for Refugee Affairs (CRA) under the Refugee Act 2012 and 2017 Regulations. Between January-June 2024, 14,653 refugee identity cards were issued. Foreigners planning to register SIMs need alien registration certificates or residence permits. The national ID itself is reserved for South Sudanese nationals.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: Approximately 20% of South Sudan's population (~12 million) have national IDs according to a 2022 official statement. UNHCR estimates ~90% of men, women and children do not possess National ID. The World Bank ID4D dataset (2017) recorded 21% official ID coverage. Low coverage is driven by conflict, displacement, remote populations, and high application costs (~$20 plus blood test and witnesses).

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: No evidence of formal independent security reviews of the national ID system. South Sudan has no data protection authority to conduct reviews. The Amnesty International 2021 report highlighted abusive surveillance by the NSS without legal safeguards, indicating absence of security oversight. No published audit or security review of the DCRNPI ID system was found.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: National ID is one of several accepted documents for SIM card registration but not mandatory exclusively. MTN South Sudan accepts: 'Payam Letter, Referendum card, Passport, Driver's license, National ID' for SIM registration. A range of documents are accepted, so the national ID is accepted but not the only option, indicating it is accepted but not mandatory.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: National ID is accepted for social services access (employment, education) but not universally mandatory. UNHCR notes ID cards 'allow people to go to school, secure work, move freely and take part in elections.' The World Bank safety net program uses ID for cash transfers. However, with ~80% lacking IDs, social services cannot strictly require them without excluding most of the population.
